posts: A donor or auditor asks why a supplier won. The answer may exist across the portal, ERP, files, email and reviewer memory. The procedure can be complete while the award record still needs reconstruction. https://www.trace-li.com/insights/the-award-was-signed-the-proof-was-not-ready

Auditability: UN OIOS found that bid evaluations at UNMISS were not timely and their documentation was inadequate. This was a final internal-audit report. Its recommendations were accepted and later recorded as implemented. https://oios.un.org/system/files/confidential-files/Reports/2024_064_pd.pdf

Financial eligibility: OLAF found an EU agency tender irregular. It stated a €7.5 million financial impact and considered the corresponding payments ineligible. This was an investigative finding and recommendations, not a final judgment or recovery. https://ec.europa.eu/olaf-report/2025/investigative-activities/protection-of-eu-funds_en.html#an-irregular-tender-procedure

Funding continuity: OLAF recommended protecting €112 million of future IPARD funding until remedial measures were in place. The source does not establish that €112 million was suspended or recovered. https://ec.europa.eu/olaf-report/2023/investigative-activities/preventing-undue-expenditure_en.html#serious-misuse-of-eu-pre-accession-agricultural-funds

Integrity exposure: the World Bank debarred a supplier for 63 months under a settlement agreement after false past-experience claims in bids for two financed projects. https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2025/06/18/world-bank-group-debars-pars-tableau-company-jsc
Four records, four procedural outcomes, one control question: could the accountable team prove the award before signing it? These are not Traceli customer stories or prevention claims.
